name: Burns
overview: Burns on the farm can come from equipment, engines, welding, or chemicals. Cool the burn quickly to limit damage.

steps.title: Cool the burn
steps.detail: Hold under cool (not ice) running water for 10–20 minutes. Or use a cool, wet cloth.

steps.title: Remove jewelry or tight items
steps.detail: Do this gently before swelling starts.

steps.title: Cover loosely
steps.detail: Use a sterile bandage or clean cloth. Don't break blisters.

steps.title: Manage pain
steps.detail: Over-the-counter pain reliever can help. Do not use butter, oil, or home remedies on burns.

when_to_seek_help: Call 911 for: burns larger than 3 inches, burns on face, hands, feet, or joints, chemical or electrical burns, or trouble breathing. Go to urgent care for blisters or burns that don't improve.
prevention_tips: Let engines and exhausts cool before servicing.
Wear gloves and eye protection when welding.
Store chemicals away from heat and flames.
